name: Knitted Pattern
basis: why: plain knitting is a lattice of V-shaped stitches; how: one pixel per stitch, yarn palette, stamped V stitch, Fair Isle border

lumenary.blurb: A jumper knitted from your picture: rows of V-shaped stitches in a handful of yarn colours, with an optional Fair Isle border.

facts.from: Hand knitting, with Nordic and Fair Isle traditions
facts.era: Knitting for about a thousand years, Fair Isle patterns from the 19th century
facts.bestOn: Bold, simple pictures with a few colours

why: Plain knitting is a lattice of V shaped stitches, each made of two plump legs of yarn, and it is wider than tall. If you draw one stitch well, with round legs, plies and a shadow, you can stamp it at every grid position and it looks like a real jumper. Colour changes between stitches then give you the picture.
how: Reduce the picture to one pixel per stitch.
Choose yarn colours by k-means and give each stitch the nearest.

For each yarn colour draw one stitch as a small picture: two ellipses tilted 0.42 radians in opposite directions with a gradient that makes them look round, slanted lines for the plies and a soft shadow.
Stamp that stitch at every position of the grid, which is about 1 to 0.74 in width to height.
Replace the top and bottom rows with a Fair Isle border, a repeating eight by seven motif of small diamonds in the darkest and lightest yarns.
history: Knitting is known from Egypt around the eleventh century, and knitted colour patterns developed in Scandinavia and the Shetland Islands. Fair Isle gets its name from a small island in Shetland, and the style became fashionable far beyond it when the Prince of Wales wore a Fair Isle pullover in 1921.
terms: The plain knitted fabric with V shaped stitches on one side.
Stranded colour knitting with small repeating patterns.
One of the strands twisted together to make yarn.
paragraphs: Plain knitting (stockinette) is a lattice of V-shaped stitches, each made of two plump legs of yarn. A knit stitch is wider than it is tall, about 1 to 0.74 here. The program draws one stitch once for every yarn colour, as a small picture: two ellipses tilted 0.42 radians in opposite directions, each filled with a gradient that is dark at the edges and bright in the middle so it looks round, with slanted lines across for the plies of the yarn and a soft shadow underneath. That sprite is then stamped at every position of the grid.

The yarn colours come from k-means on a picture with one pixel per stitch; each stitch takes the nearest. The Fair Isle border replaces the top and bottom rows (up to eight of each) with a repeating eight-by-seven motif, a lattice of small diamonds followed by a blank row and a solid row, knitted in the darkest and lightest of the chosen yarns, in the manner of a Nordic jumper.

equations.note: Stitch width, height and number of rows for n stitches across.
Each of the two legs is an ellipse of these radii.

presets.text: More stitches across give a finer fabric.
Three yarn colours make it look like a classic jumper.
Turn off the Fair Isle border for a plain panel.
